subject: Request: temporary rate-limit & quota exception for FastCommerce product launch
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@fastcommerce.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch week request: temporary rate-limit increase

Hi Karthik,

Quick note — we have a hard launch planned for May 10 at 10:00 PDT for FastCommerce new checkout flow. Our SREs ran a spike test and are concerned we'll hit the default per-customer rate limits right away.

Can Redwood temporarily increase our request quota and burst capacity for the 24–48 hour launch window? Attaching our preliminary forecast (fastcommerce_launch_forecast_v1.xlsx). Key asks:
- Temporary RPS increase (peak planning)
- Larger token quota for generation endpoints
- Contact for on-call if we see errors

We'd like to confirm this ASAP so we can finalize the rollout schedule.

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Director, Platform Ops
FastCommerce

Attachment: fastcommerce_launch_forecast_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week request: temporary rate-limit increase

Hi Emma — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. Looping in David (product) and Rishi (infra) to confirm what we can do safely and what we need from your side.

Questions up front so we can size the exception properly:
- Confirm launch start time and expected peak window (local timezone).
- Expected concurrency (peak RPS) and avg tokens per request.
- Are you calling streaming endpoints or standard complete calls?
- Any expected change in prompt/response lengths during promotional spikes?

We can often provide a temporary quota bump + burst capacity, but we need the token math and an operational runbook from you. If you can fill the attached template (launch_traffic_template.csv) and return by EOD tomorrow, we should be able to commit to a plan.

I'll aim to get an approval from infra for a 3x burst increase for a limited window once we have numbers.

-Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: launch_traffic_template.csv (please complete)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week request: temporary rate-limit increase

Karthik / team — can you ask FastCommerce to include the following in the template? If any of these numbers are fuzzy we need conservative margins.

1) Peak concurrent requests (RPS) per endpoint (generation, chat, embeddings).
2) Average prompt tokens in and average generated tokens out (we need tokens/minute).
3) Expected session duration and how many parallel user sessions you expect.
4) Any retry/backoff logic in client — retries can multiply load.
5) Confirmation whether caching/prefix reuse is possible on your end (we can enable KV/prefix caching to dramatically cut tokens).

Operational asks from infra:
- We may pre-warm a reserved capacity pool (Dedicated burst) for 72 hours around launch.
- We will instrument per-route token-level tracing for the window to catch regressions.

If they provide numbers by EOD tomorrow, I'll draft an exception plan.

-David
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@fastcommerce.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: launch-ops@fastcommerce.com
Date: Fri, 8 May 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week request: temporary rate-limit increase

David/Karthik — thanks, attached is the completed template with more granular numbers. Highlighting the important pieces here:

- Launch start: 2026-05-10 10:00 PDT; peak window: 10:00–13:00 PDT (3 hours) with elevated tail to 18:00 PDT.
- Peak generation endpoint RPS (expected): 1,200 RPS across our region (mostly US).
- Avg tokens/request: 850 tokens in + 400 tokens out (approx).
- Estimated tokens/sec at peak: ~1,200 RPS * 1,250 tokens ~ 1.5M tokens/minute (~25k tokens/sec).
- We're using standard generate endpoints (not streaming) for the checkout personalization.
- We do have some reuse of prompts, but not reliably; we can add simple prefix caching on our side if you recommend it.
- Retries: client will have exponential backoff; expected <5% retries.

Also attaching our final forecast (fastcommerce_launch_forecast_v1.xlsx updated). Let us know what you need for the runbook.

Thanks,
Emma

Attachment: fastcommerce_launch_forecast_v1.xlsx (updated)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2026 06:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week request: temporary rate-limit increase

Team — after reviewing the numbers and the forecast, infra is OK to support a temporary exception with the following plan:

- Window: 2026-05-10 09:00 PDT to 2026-05-12 09:00 PDT (48 hours).
- Rate-limit bump: default per-customer RPS -> 1,500 RPS (sustained), burst capacity allowed up to 3,000 RPS for short spikes.
- Token quotas: increase token budget for their account by 10x for the window; we'll place a hard cap and notify if they exceed.
- Reserved capacity: pre-warm 2 dedicated instances for the 72-hour window starting 2026-05-10 06:00 PDT.
- Observability: enable token-level tracing and per-route dashboards; alerts to infra on error-rate >1.5% or 5xx increase.

Operational requirements for FastCommerce before we flip the switch:
- Sign and return the quick runbook acknowledgement (temp_sla_exception.pdf) with emergency contact and escalation matrix.
- Implement simple prefix caching and remove aggressive client-side retries during peak.
- Provide a Slack escalation channel and an on-call phone number to reach their SRE.

I'll add an internal runbook and escalate to SRE on-call at 08:30 PDT. Karthik — please confirm you communicated the plan to Emma and get the signed acknowledgement.

-Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: temp_sla_exception.pdf (quick acknowledgement)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week request: temporary rate-limit increase

Emma — good news: infra has provisionally approved a temporary exception. Summary and next steps below. Please reply ACK with the signed acknowledgement PDF and confirmation of the Slack channel.

Summary of what we will apply for FastCommerce (2026-05-10 09:00 PDT -> 2026-05-12 09:00 PDT):
- Sustained RPS bump to 1,500 RPS; burst allowed to 3,000 RPS for brief spikes.
- Token budget increased 10x for the window (hard cap enforced).
- Reserved pre-warmed capacity + enhanced tracing and per-route dashboards.
- Alerts: infra will page if error-rate >1.5%.

FastCommerce operational asks (you):
- Return signed temp_sla_exception.pdf (attached) with emergency contact.
- Enable prefix caching on your client; remove aggressive retries.
- Use streaming where possible for large responses (we can help with quick changes).
- Join the SRE/Infra channel: #fastcommerce-launch (please create / invite us).

On-call details for Redwood during the window will be shared in the runbook link: https://app.redwood.com/runbooks/fastcommerce-temp-increase

Once we have your ACK and signed doc, infra will flip the exception at 09:00 PDT. Good luck with the launch — we’ll monitor closely and stand by.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123
